# Index — Alphabetical {#sec-index-alpha .unnumbered}

Every defined or coined term in the lexicon, ordered A–Z. This is the
alphabetical view of the [Terminology](terminology.qmd) chapter
(§-@sec-terminology), which holds the same set grouped by subject. Use this one when you
know the word, that one when you want the neighborhood it belongs to.

Each entry gives a short gloss and two links: **§-@sec-terminology** for the definition, and,
where a chapter develops the term, the section that does so. The built-in
site search (top of every page) complements both, since search finds a word
anywhere in the prose, while this list is the curated set of terms the
document actually defines.

Zone codes **A0–A5** are grouped under **A**; farming axis positions **S1–S5**
under **S**.

---

## A {.unnumbered}

**A0 — Rooftop** — arrays on buildings, and by extension carports and canopies, which take no ground at all: no siting latitude, no ground layer, and no farming axis position; the transect's origin rather than a point on it — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-a0) · [The Zones](scale-transect.qmd#sec-zones)

**A1 — Farmstead** — <100 kW, behind-the-meter, single owner-operator, existing farm labor — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-a1) · [The Zones](scale-transect.qmd#sec-zones)

**A2 — Commercial** — 100 kW–1 MW, behind-meter to distribution, landowner with possibly one lease counterparty — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-a2) · [The Zones](scale-transect.qmd#sec-zones)

**A3 — Community** — 1–5 MW, distribution / community solar, multi-party, purpose-built ground management — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-a3) · [The Zones](scale-transect.qmd#sec-zones)

**A4 — Utility** — 5–50 MW, developer-led institutional capital, contract-enterprise management — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-a4) · [The Zones](scale-transect.qmd#sec-zones)

**A5 — Complex** — 50 MW+, transmission, utility/IPP, contract enterprise at ranch scale — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-a5) · [The Zones](scale-transect.qmd#sec-zones)

**Agricultural production** — design pressure: keep working land working — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-agricultural-production) · [The pressures](design-pressures.qmd#sec-pressures)

**Agriculture and soils function** — restorative function: what the array does for farming, on its ground and the fields around it, via pollination, pest regulation, forage and shelter, and the lease that keeps the operation running; not the farming axis restated — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-fn-agricultural) · [Agriculture and soils](restorative-functions.qmd#sec-fn-agricultural)

**Agrisolar** — agroenergy specific to photovoltaics; the lexicon's working umbrella (after NCAT's AgriSolar Clearinghouse usage), broadened to be neutral across the farming axis — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-agrisolar)

**Agrivoltaics** — crop or livestock production within the array footprint (S1–S2); *cf.* agrophotovoltaics, photovoltaic agriculture — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-agrivoltaics)

**Agroenergy** — energy infrastructure designed to interact intentionally with agricultural or ecological land function; umbrella term — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-agroenergy)

**Archetype** — a way the design pressures have been resolved at a particular scale zone and sharing position —  [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-archetype) · [Archetypal Forms](archetypal-forms.qmd)

## B {.unnumbered}

**Bare conversion** — ordinary ground converted with the farm operation ended: the same ground fact as S3 without the restorative one. The non-restorative baseline the axis is read against, not a position on it — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-bare-conversion) · [The positions](farming-axis.qmd#sec-positions)

**Benefit delivery** — which route a function's benefit takes to whoever receives it: in place, along a connection (water, living things, or institutions), or by preservation; the route, not the distance, decides who can check the claim — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-benefit-delivery) · [Where benefits are delivered](restorative-functions.qmd#sec-benefit-range)

## C {.unnumbered}

**Carrying capacity** — season-long forage the land sustains over time; a grazing design variable — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-carrying-capacity) · [Worked example: grazing](scale-transect.qmd#sec-grazing)

**Coexistence** — retired as a position name; *see* S3 — Ordinary-land siting, the center of the farming axis, neither sharing nor sparing — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-s3) · [The positions](farming-axis.qmd#sec-positions)

**Co-benefit** — the field's usual word for a restorative function; recorded but not adopted, because its grammar demotes what it names to something arriving alongside the real objective — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-cobenefit)

**Co-location** — panels and a land use share a parcel without functional interdependence; *cf.* integration — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-colocation-integration)

**Community & economic function** — the socioeconomic restorative function: durable local income, livability, and whether the burdens and the benefits land on the same people, built for the host community; the outcomes footprint's Communities domain read as an outcome, distinct from the social-license pressure and community-benefit lever — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-fn-community) · [Community and economy](restorative-functions.qmd#sec-fn-community)

**Community acceptance and benefit** — design pressure: secure and sustain community acceptance *and* community benefit — two forces that can come apart, held in one pressure — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-community-acceptance) · [The pressures](design-pressures.qmd#sec-pressures)

**Community Benefit** — instruments returning value to the host community (CBA/HCA, PILOT, good-neighbor payments, community-solar subscription, co-ownership, decommissioning bond); distinct from acceptance — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-community-benefit)

**Connectivity** — whether organisms can move into, through, and out of a site; designed at four scales, from fencing and mown strips to whether a regional fleet falls within dispersal distance — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-connectivity) · [Ecology](restorative-functions.qmd#sec-fn-biodiversity)

**Contract grazing** — grazing delivered as a contracted vegetation-management service by a party who does not live on site — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-contract-grazing) · [Worked example: grazing](scale-transect.qmd#sec-grazing)

**Contract-led** — restoration mode: the work is done in the lease, the ordinance, or the benefit agreement rather than anywhere on the site; the mode the community and economic function runs on — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-contract-led) · [Community and economy](restorative-functions.qmd#sec-fn-community)

**Cost and financing** — design pressure: minimize what the project costs to build and what it costs to finance — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-cost-financing) · [The pressures](design-pressures.qmd#sec-pressures)
## D {.unnumbered}

**Decommissioning / Repowering / Reversibility** — end-of-life questions: removing and restoring, replacing modules, and how completely the prior land use can return — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-decommissioning)

**Delivery by preservation** — the mode in which nothing moves and the benefit is ground nearby that stayed as it was; proximate, because development pressure is local, but counterfactual rather than observed — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-displaced-benefit) · [Where benefits are delivered](restorative-functions.qmd#sec-benefit-range)

**Design import** — the characteristic regional failure: carrying a resolution from the region where it was demonstrated into one whose factors differ; grid and market demands is the usual vehicle — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-design-import) · [What follows](design-pressures.qmd#sec-rg-consequences)

**Design levers** — the six kinds of decision a project can make, and the only things anyone can change: scale, siting, structure, management, ownership, contracts — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-design-levers) · [Design Levers](design-levers.qmd)

**Design pressures** — the competing forces every site must resolve; unlike axes they have direction, conflict, and advocates — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-design-pressures) · [Design Pressures](design-pressures.qmd)

**Design tension** — what a resolution of the design pressures leaves unresolved; never nil, so the question is how much remains and who carries it, and the settings that leave least are the ones that recur — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-design-tension) · [Where the pressures collide](design-pressures.qmd#sec-conflicts)

**Diffuse fraction** — the share of irradiance arriving as diffuse rather than direct-beam light; higher under cloud, non-directional, and most of what a ground layer lives on — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-diffuse-fraction) · [Six factors](design-pressures.qmd#sec-rg-resource)

**Dual Use** — production-based criterion: active agricultural production in the footprint across the project life (AFT's definition); S1–S2 — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-dual-use)

## E {.unnumbered}

**Ecological function** — restorative function: what can live on the ground and what can move through it; habitat from the ground layer up, plus connectivity — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-fn-biodiversity) · [Ecology](restorative-functions.qmd#sec-fn-biodiversity)

**Ecovoltaics** — solar development incorporating ecological understanding into array design and management, co-prioritizing ecosystem function with generation; its ecological ground layer is a restorative function rather than an axis position, most often built at S3 — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-ecovoltaics)

**End-of-life responsibility** — a design pressure: minimize the residual footprint and preserve the option to return the ground to its prior use — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-end-of-life) · [The pressures](design-pressures.qmd#sec-pressures)

**Energy yield** — design pressure: maximize energy per unit land — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-energy-yield) · [The pressures](design-pressures.qmd#sec-pressures)

## F {.unnumbered}

**Feasible wedge** — the feasible region across scale and sharing: the sharing edge runs flat across the whole transect, the sparing edge opens with scale, and only S4 thins toward A5 — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-feasible-wedge) · [Which positions scale allows](farming-axis.qmd#sec-wedge)

**Footprint** — land physically occupied by racking, panels, and access infrastructure; paired with influence zone — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-footprint-influence)

## G {.unnumbered}

**Grid and market demands** — design pressure: satisfy the criteria of whoever buys the power, attributes, or tax position — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-grid-market) · [The pressures](design-pressures.qmd#sec-pressures)

**Ground Coverage Ratio (GCR)** — ratio of module area to ground area; the array's density; the number behind the row-geometry ↔ ground-layer coupling — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-gcr)

**Ground Layer** — whatever occupies the surface beneath and between panels; primary carrier of restorative function; *syn.* understory, ground cover — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-ground-layer)

## H {.unnumbered}

**Hydrologic function** — restorative function: water quantity (infiltration, recharge, soil moisture, and at scale consumptive use retired from a basin's budget) and water quality by two routes needing opposite ground, avoided loading on the ground that leaches and interception on the flow path below it — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-fn-hydrologic) · [Water](restorative-functions.qmd#sec-fn-hydrologic)

## I {.unnumbered}

**Influence Zone** — the larger, typically asymmetric area whose hydrology, microclimate, soil, or wildlife movement is measurably affected — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-footprint-influence)

**Integration** — functional interdependence — panel height set by livestock clearance, spacing by forage light, tracking by photosynthetic timing — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-colocation-integration)

## L {.unnumbered}

**Land Equivalent Ratio (LER)** — standard dual-use productivity metric; handles the non-production ground layers of S3–S5 poorly — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-ler)

**Land sharing** — production continues on the ground the array occupies; the sharing wing of the axis (S1–S2). Borrowed from conservation ecology — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-farming-axis) · [The Farming Axis](farming-axis.qmd)

**Land sparing** — ground comes out of production so other ground can be left alone; the sparing wing of the axis (S4–S5). Borrowed from conservation ecology — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-farming-axis) · [The Farming Axis](farming-axis.qmd)

## M {.unnumbered}

**Management-led** — restoration mode: placement is a given; ground cover, grazing regime, and operational schedule carry everything — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-management-led) · [The five modes](restoration-modes.qmd#sec-lv-mode)

**Marginal / Previously Disturbed Land** — the low-value ground that low-productivity siting (S4) presupposes: low-yielding cropland, reclaimed mine land, landfills, brownfields ("brightfields") — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-marginal-land)

**Module Technology** — the panel as a lever: monofacial/bifacial, vertical bifacial, semitransparent, spectrally selective — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-module-technology)

**Multi-use solar** — the field's competing umbrella (Merheb et al. 2025), covering agrivoltaics, rangevoltaics, and ecovoltaics; narrower than *agrisolar* as used here, which also covers S3–S5 — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-agrisolar)

## O {.unnumbered}

**Operations and maintenance** — design pressure: minimize management burden across a 25–40 year asset life — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-operations-maintenance) · [The pressures](design-pressures.qmd#sec-pressures)

**Overhead and interspace systems** — the engineering standards' hardware typology (DIN SPEC 91434; NREL/InSPIRE): modules above the working surface, or low with the crop between rows; classifies structure, where an archetype classifies the resolution of pressures — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-overhead-interspace) · [Archetypal Forms](archetypal-forms.qmd)

**Ownership-led** — restoration mode: the work is done by who holds the asset, with no agreement needed because the parties were never opposed; strongest at A1–A2 and unavailable once the owner is absentee — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-ownership-led) · [The five modes](restoration-modes.qmd#sec-lv-mode)

## P {.unnumbered}

**Policy and permission** — design pressure: satisfy the rules that decide whether the project happens at all, and the subsidies that decide what pays; the one pressure whose direction the jurisdiction sets — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-policy-permission) · [The pressures](design-pressures.qmd#sec-pressures)

**Pore Space** — the three-dimensional volume between modules and between modules and ground; frames clearance as habitat and working space — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-pore-space)

## R {.unnumbered}

**Rangevoltaics** — grazing under and between the panels, S1 on ground that was already pasture and S2 on former cropland; the field's ecological-literature name for solar grazing, workable with sheep but not with goats, cattle, or horses; *syn.* solar grazing — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-rangevoltaics) · [Worked example: grazing](scale-transect.qmd#sec-grazing)

**Regional calibration** — a restatement of the lexicon's indicative values for a particular region: capacity bands, absent zones, the binding constraint, the positions realistically open — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-regional-calibration) · [A worked calibration](design-pressures.qmd#sec-rg-us)

**Regional factors** — the six spatial factors a region is read by: resource, grid operator, aridity, latitude, cropping system, irrigation — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-regional-factors) · [Six factors](design-pressures.qmd#sec-rg-factors)

**Regionality** — the claim that the design pressures resolve differently in different places, because the factors that weight them vary across space; the vocabulary is constant, the weights are not — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-regionality) · [The same pressures, weighted by place](design-pressures.qmd#sec-regionality)

**Restoration mode** — which design lever carried the restorative work — Siting-led, Structure-led, Management-led, Ownership-led, or Contract-led — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-restoration-mode) · [The five modes](restoration-modes.qmd#sec-lv-mode)

**Restorative** — the frame of the whole lexicon: ground-layer function as a design objective co-equal with generation — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-restorative)

**Restorative goals** — design pressure: make ecological, hydrological, and economic resilience co-equal with generation — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-restorative-goals) · [The pressures](design-pressures.qmd#sec-pressures)

**Restorative function** — a restorative capacity a project can be designed to deliver, reachable across many structural positions; two biophysical (water, ecology) plus one agricultural (agriculture and soils) and one socioeconomic (community and economy) — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-restorative-function) · [Restorative Functions](restorative-functions.qmd)

## S {.unnumbered}

**S0 — Created agriculture** — a farm takes something off ground that carried no agricultural use before the array; the one position that records a use beginning rather than one displaced — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-s0) · [The positions](farming-axis.qmd#sec-positions)

**S1 — Primary agriculture** — the agricultural use continues essentially as it was, with the array added over or between it — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-s1) · [The positions](farming-axis.qmd#sec-positions)

**S2 — Secondary agriculture** — a farm still works the ground, at a lower value than it carried before; grazing on former cropland, forage, hay, hives — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-s2) · [The positions](farming-axis.qmd#sec-positions)

**S3 — Ordinary-land siting** — neither sharing nor sparing: the array takes ordinary ground outright and the revenue sustains the farm enterprise holding it, so the restoration is socioeconomic rather than biophysical; the center of the axis — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-s3) · [The positions](farming-axis.qmd#sec-positions)

**S4 — Low-productivity siting** — the array takes ground already idle, marginal, or chronically low-yielding, so nothing in production was displaced to build it; arrays on buildings take no ground and hold no position (A0) — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-s4) · [The positions](farming-axis.qmd#sec-positions)

**S5 — Impaired-land siting** — the array takes ground that carried a measurable off-site burden (low yields, high runoff, nutrient export, irrigation draw beyond the aquifer's budget), or that sits where such a burden can be intercepted — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-s5) · [The positions](farming-axis.qmd#sec-positions)

**outcomes footprint** — a whole-project reading across four domains (Communities, Agriculture, Water, Ecology), each running from causing harm at the center, through avoiding harm, out to promoting benefit at the rim; the ring is a zero point, not a pass mark — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-scale-footprint) · [The outcomes footprint](restorative-functions.qmd#sec-scale)

**Scale Transect** — a single gradient from farmstead to complex that most other terms are read against; defined by covarying bundles, not capacity — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-scale-transect) · [The Scale Transect](scale-transect.qmd)

**Screening** — management of the array's outward visual presence (setbacks, buffers, berms, fencing, glint/glare); acts on the visual portion of the influence zone; dual-function — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-screening)

**Setback** — the ground held open between the array and the property line, road, or dwelling; the dimension local ordinances fix most often, and where screening gets planted — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-setback)

**Siting Axis** — retired as the axis name; *see* Farming Axis — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-farming-axis) · [The Farming Axis](farming-axis.qmd)

**Farming Axis** — the scale-orthogonal dimension: whether the array shares land with production (*land sharing*), spares land by taking ground out of it (*land sparing*), or neither; five positions centered on S3 — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-farming-axis) · [The Farming Axis](farming-axis.qmd)

**Siting latitude** — the designer's freedom over where the array goes; peaks at A2–A3, bounded by the parcel at A1 and by the land market and grid topology at A5 — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-siting-latitude) · [Scale constrains design leverage](restoration-modes.qmd#sec-siting-latitude)

**Siting-led** — restoration mode: the restorative work is done by the choice of ground; requires A2–A3 latitude — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-siting-led) · [The five modes](restoration-modes.qmd#sec-lv-mode)

**Solar grazing** — *see* Rangevoltaics — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-rangevoltaics)

**Stocking density** — instantaneous animals per unit area at a moment; diverges from carrying capacity — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-stocking-density) · [Worked example: grazing](scale-transect.qmd#sec-grazing)

**Structure-led** — restoration mode: array geometry is the instrument — clearance, row spacing, module transmissivity — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-structure-led) · [The five modes](restoration-modes.qmd#sec-lv-mode)

## T {.unnumbered}

**Tracking Schedule & Curtailment** — operational-regime levers: how the array is steered through the day, and deliberate output reduction — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-tracking-curtailment)

## V {.unnumbered}

**Viewshed** — the ground from which the array can be seen; the part of the influence zone that reaches people rather than water, soil, or wildlife, and what screening acts on — [Terminology](terminology.qmd#term-viewshed)
